correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs every quantity from explicit hypotheses. The cited affine chart turns the upper truncation into \(d+1\) pairwise disjoint cube caps of threshold \(t=(dn-m)/2\). Exact inclusion-exclusion yields the cap volume and therefore formula (1). Only the \(j\)-th positive-part term changes branch at \(m_j=(d-2j)n\), giving the stated \(d\)-th derivative jump. Separately, the Hadamard centers have mutual Hamming distance \((d+1)/2\), so the relevant Hamming layers are disjoint; direct layer and edge counts give the full vertex formulas and exactly \((d+1)\binom{d}{j}\) resonance vertices. The published local cone proves those and only those resonance vertices are nonsimple, and its extreme rays give degree \((j+1)(d-j)\). No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result attaches an exact analytic signature to every smoothness transition in a current Hadamard-truncation family: the size of the first discontinuous volume derivative equals the exact number of nonsimple vertices. It also supplies a universal vertex-count phase diagram and local degrees, independent of the Hadamard equivalence class. These are natural structural invariants of the same geometry used in the source's smoothness and normality analysis, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known table.
